authority_policy: All live authority flags default false.
This index never grants send, submit, browser, model, worker, or workflow authority.
capability_record_policy: Every capability declares inputs, outputs, status, authority, and next safe move.
Future-gated and contract-only records cannot claim live execution.
doctrine: Generic capabilities are reusable interfaces, not workflow fixtures.
Fixtures prove behavior but have no execution authority.
doctrine_gate_policy: Human dignity, sensitive data, approval, and tenant-scope policies wrap consequential capabilities.
Automation/labor/pricing/data extraction contexts require doctrine checks.
fixture_policy: Fixtures cannot satisfy authority gates or prove live provider availability.
intent_interpreter_policy: Future LM interpreters may query this map but cannot write canonical truth.
Machine intent candidates still require deterministic validation.
lifecycle_policy: Generated code without tests enters BUILT_UNVALIDATED.
Passing tests without authority remains VALIDATED_NON_EXECUTING.
LIVE_IMPLEMENTED requires explicit authority profile and receipt-backed validation.
compiler.next_safe_move: Use this index to route questions, identify gaps, and validate candidate intent without executing anything.
portability_policy: Generic definitions must be user-agnostic and task-agnostic.
Workflow/client examples stay in binding or fixture records.
Task-specific labels must not become core taxonomy.
privacy_boundary: No broad folder scans or external system probes.
promotion_gate_policy: Promotion requires code refs, tests, read-models, receipts, authority profile, and doctrine checks.
No candidate can promote itself or become live from LM output alone.
proposal_candidate_policy: Proposal candidates are quarantined suggestions for missing capability.
Candidates are not generic capabilities, not executable, and not trusted.
Candidates are ignored by active routing until promotion gates pass.
source_scan_policy: Use safe file/module name inspection and existing deterministic definitions.
Do not inspect private bodies, credentials, external systems, or runtime queues.
Do not infer live authority from a filename or read-model.
tenant_scope_policy: Generic capability definitions may be visible when safe.
Workflow bindings and fixtures require tenant/client filtering.
Invalid tenant scope returns no tenant/client-specific bindings.
workflow_binding_policy: Bindings map generic capability refs to concrete workflow implementations.
Bindings may include client/workflow fixture labels and must keep scope explicit.

doctrine_gates.next_safe_move: Run dignity/impact review before consequential automation or data extraction.
Use refs, tokens, and metadata only unless a protected lane explicitly permits more.
Require exact approval receipts and proof refs before any future action adapter.
Filter workflow bindings by tenant/client scope and expose only safe generic definitions.
